items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: the first picture we did there was with Ann Miller

ctx.x: an honor; for a white musician or a black musician; whatever you were -- that was really steady. You didn't have to worry about where you were gonna get work; you pick up your check every week, and it was considered the best job in town to be on the staff.

And so we had one out there, anyway, so I was there, and I worked on -- the first picture, I remember very well, the first picture we did there was with Ann Miller. I was trying to think of the title of it, but my first day there, I have to play 5 timpanies. They had written a part that the timpany had the melody, and the whole thing was built around the timpanies, you know, but I told you before about my extreme cockiness, and I was a stickler for getting places on time.

And being a percussionist, if the call was 9 o'clock, I would be there at 8 o'clock, and so being my first day, I was a little apprehensive, and wondering what I was gonna have to play. So I imagine I got there about an hour and a half ahead of time, and so I got there early enough to look at this book and see these timpany parts, you know, really hard!
